cohort: The study included 378 Jordanian women in their second or third trimester of pregnancy, who were either primiparous or para-one.
finding: The study found that preference leaned more strongly toward vaginal delivery over cesarean section, and higher knowledge levels and decision-making involvement were observed among women receiving prenatal care at university-affiliated or private facilities, as well as those with better knowledge and more positive preferences toward vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: The majority of participants (57.2%) showed a stronger preference toward vaginal delivery over cesarean section, and decision-making involvement was higher among women with better knowledge and more positive preferences toward vaginal delivery.
cross-section timing: during the second or third trimester of pregnancy
